subject: [ACTION] Temporary moratorium request: AuroraBPE family - BPE endianness tokenization mismatch
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora.patel@acme-ml.com>
Date: Mon, 23 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [ACTION] Temporary moratorium request: AuroraBPE family - BPE endianness tokenization mismatch

Team,

We saw a set of repeated tokenization deltas while running the AuroraBPE v1.4 candidate across our standard regression prompt set. Symptoms: identical prompts are producing different token sequences compared to v1.2 (leading to shifted generation and off-by-one decode errors in a small but material percent of requests). Marcus attached a compact diff (aurora-bpe-diff.patch) and example failing prompts (tokenization-failures-samples.csv).

Impact summary:
- User-visible regressions on short-form prompts (~2% failure on our churned prompt set).
- Downstream scoring and reranking pipelines observe alignment drift because token offsets changed.
- Client SDKs that rely on exact token alignment for function-calling note mismatched argument spans.

Ask: I propose a temporary moratorium on onboarding new AuroraBPE-derived variants (including v1.4 and any immediate forks) until we validate the tokenization contract across: sequence length behavior, BPE merge ordering/endianness, and byte-level normalization. Specifically:
1) Karthik — please pin serving traffic for the AuroraBPE family to v1.2 (current stable) for 72 hours to stop any rollout activity. Provide the pin command and any CI gating checks needed.
2) Marcus — can you run the tokenization diff harness across the full 10k prompt corpus and surface a short report (counts by category: start-offset shifts, split/merge changes, normalization divergences)? Attachments include a minimal patch and samples.
3) Laura — can you map this into the product rollout calendar and flag any customers in active canary?

I want to avoid a wider rollout pause if possible, but given the potential for user-facing regressions and the tight coupling to downstream spans, we should be conservative. If we need to escalate to legal/SLA owners we will.

Thanks — I.

--
Irene Choi
Head of Product Operations | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora.patel@acme-ml.com>
Date: Mon, 23 May 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [ACTION] Temporary moratorium request: AuroraBPE family - BPE endianness tokenization mismatch

Irene — acknowledged.

We can lock the AuroraBPE route to v1.2 immediately; operationally that is a single api-config flip and a short-lived feature-flag pin. I'll perform the pin and emit the rollback/pin commands here once done (I expect sub-15m to enact, barring any in-flight deployment conflicts). A couple notes:
- We should confirm that client SDKs won't attempt to re-tokenize older cached payloads; pinning server-side won't fix persisted client-side encodings.
- Recommend a canary first: pin prod route but allow 1% traffic to an isolated canary that runs v1.4 in parallel with strict telemetry on token-delta counts. If canary is clear after 24h we can revisit.

Marcus — can you produce the counts mentioned and scope whether a normalization patch on the tokenizer (vs model artifact) is the root cause? If it's a model artifact we need a model patch from Acme.

Executing pin now; I'll follow up with the CLI snippet and confirmation ID.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior SRE, Inference Platform | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora.patel@acme-ml.com>
Date: Mon, 23 May 2027 11:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [ACTION] Temporary moratorium request: AuroraBPE family - BPE endianness tokenization mismatch

On Mon, May 23, 2027 at 09:12 AM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> We saw a set of repeated tokenization deltas while running the AuroraBPE v1.4 candidate...

Quick update from the tokenization harness: initial run over the 10k regression corpus shows three buckets:
- normalization differences (NFKC vs NFC effects) ~0.9% of samples
- BPE merge-order/endianness shifts ~1.1% of samples
- whitespace/byte-normalization edge-cases ~0.3% of samples

I attached a trimmed diff (aurora-bpe-diff.patch) showing the merge order change that causes a single-token vs two-token split on certain multi-byte punctuation sequences. That lines up with the off-by-one decode patterns we saw.

Actionable:
- Recommend pining to v1.2 immediately (Karthik — proceed).
- I'll prepare a detailed report by EOD tomorrow with sample counts by customer, and include a short harness that Acme can run to validate the patched tokenizer.
- If Acme provides a tokenizer-only patch we can evaluate whether a server-side pre-tokenizer shim can reconcile differences without rolling model weights.

I'll also add smoke tests to the staging canary to detect regressions during future variant intake.

-Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Developer Experience Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Nora Patel <nora.patel@acme-ml.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [ACTION] Temporary moratorium request: AuroraBPE family - BPE endianness tokenization mismatch

Hi all — thank you for flagging and for the initial analysis. Apologies for the customer impact. I've pulled in the tokenizer team at Acme; early take: a non-deterministic merge-order change slipped into the v1.4 BPE builder when we adjusted internal sorting to improve build speed. That explains the observed endianness-style shifts.

We will:
- Produce a tokenizer-only patch by EOD tomorrow that restores deterministic merge ordering and run it against the harness in Marcus's attachment.
- Share a canonical test vector set and a small script so Redwood can validate server-side before any further rollout.

Request: if you can pin to v1.2 and block v1.4 variants for 72 hours (as suggested) we will prioritize the patch and give you a clear timeline for re-ingest.

I'll send the patch and a short verification README as soon as we have it.

Thanks — Nora

--
Nora Patel
Engineering Lead, Tokenization | Acme ML
nora.patel@acme-ml.com
